classification.difficultyReason: Identify the angle opposite the longest side before applying cosine rule.

content.prompt: A triangle has side lengths $10\text{ m}$, $7\text{ m}$, and $13\text{ m}$. Find the largest angle, to one decimal place.

answer.worked:
The largest angle is opposite the longest side, $13\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos\theta&=\frac{10^2+7^2-13^2}{2(10)(7)}\\[8pt]\theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac17\right)\\[8pt]\theta&\approx98.2^\circ\end{align*}$$
